key_insight: Encoding seasonal structure helps quantum data-reuploading models retain forecasting accuracy as circuit depth increases, while standard value-based encodings degrade.
engineering_relevance: Structure-aware encoding offers a practical design strategy for deeper quantum time-series models, though circuit noise and optimization remain constraints.
method: Use fidelity-based quantum geometry to analyze how repeated encodings distinguish recurrent inputs.
Encode observation magnitude and seasonal phase in distinct Bloch-sphere coordinates using fixed or adaptive schemes.
Evaluate 14-month lag forecasts across reuploading depths L = 1–6.
evidence_signal: On monthly ERA5-Land precipitation from a semi-arid East African region, adaptive seasonal encodings preserved temporal and spectral structure in ideal simulations; seasonal models remained competitive with ARIMA, random forests, and LSTMs.
watch_item: Noisy simulations limited deeper circuits, and evaluation in one representative region does not establish broad generalization or quantum advantage.
paper_title: Quantum machine learning geospatial time-series by seasonal encoding
